If I remove the `@font-face` rules, all those font-family names become undefined → fall back to... their **next** fallback in each declaration. Many declarations are like `font-family:'Noto Sans SC:Medium','Noto Sans SC',sans-serif` → would fall to `sans-serif` (system). But some like `'Plus Jakarta Sans:SemiBold',sans-serif` also fall to sans-serif. And page's `font-family` line 34 has full system stack.

So removing @font-face alone would make everything fall to `sans-serif` (browser default sans), which is a system font — acceptable, but the **page** rule already has a nicer explicit system stack. Best approach per "用系统默认字体":
1. Remove the 6 `@font-face` rules.
2. Replace the custom font-family names throughout with the system stack so text uses the well-defined system fonts (not just bare `sans-serif`).

But that's many edits.

tool_input.content:
import re

files = [
    r"D:\repository\苏住房防汛C端-wt-sysfont\src\styles\theme.css",
    r"D:\repository\苏住房防汛C端-wt-sysfont\src\styles\ref8443.css",
]

customs = [
    "'Noto Sans SC:Regular'",
    "'Noto Sans SC:Medium'",
    "'Noto Sans SC:Bold'",
    "'Noto Sans SC'",
    "'Plus Jakarta Sans:Regular'",
    "'Plus Jakarta Sans:Medium'",
    "'Plus Jakarta Sans:SemiBold'",
    "'Plus Jakarta Sans'",
]

def clean_family_value(val: str) -> str:
    parts = [p.strip() for p in val.split(',')]
    kept = []
    for p in parts:
        if p in customs:
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    # dedup preserving order
    seen = set(); out = []
    for p in kept:
        if p not in seen:
            seen.add(p); out.append(p)
    if not out or out == ['sans-serif']:
        return 'sans-serif'
    return ','.join(out)

for path in files:
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        text = f.read()
    orig = text

    # 1) remove @font-face lines (only in theme.css)
    if path.endswith('theme.css'):
        lines = text.split('\n')
        lines = [ln for ln in lines if not ln.lstrip().startswith('@font-face')]
        text = '\n'.join(lines)

    # 2) rewrite every font-family:<value> declaration
    def repl(m):
        prefix = m.group(1)   # 'font-family:'
        val = m.group(2)
        return prefix + clean_family_value(val)

    # match font-family: up to ; or } , value may include commas & quotes, no ; or }
    text = re.sub(r'(font-family:)([^;}]+)', repl, text)

    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        f.write(text)
    print(f"{path}: changed={orig!=text} len {len(orig)}->{len(text)}")
print("done")
